meta.description: One red-green slice, three nodes: write a failing test for a named behavior, implement the minimum to pass, then an independent verifier re-runs the suite fresh. For small, provable feature steps.

repo_dir.desc: absolute path of the git checkout to work in

slice.desc: ONE behavior, phrased so a test can pin it

test_cmd.desc: one command line, run from repo root, whose exit 0 means the suite is green

graph.name: test-first-feature-slice
graph.description: Test-first delivery of ONE feature slice. SEED CONTRACT (run_context map, ALL THREE keys required, plain text, no braces): 'repo_dir' = absolute path of the checkout; 'slice' = exactly ONE behavior, phrased so a test can pin it (surfaces at most one slice per run - a list is a queue you dispatch twice); 'test_cmd' = the repo's own command line that runs the relevant tests from the repo root and exits nonzero on failure. LAUNCH: run from:'general/test-first-feature-slice' run_context:{'repo_dir':'/abs/path','slice':'<one behavior>','test_cmd':'<repo test command>'}. NODE MAP: red (write the failing test, prove it fails for the RIGHT reason) -> green (minimum implementation to pass, never weaken the test) -> verify (fresh independent re-run of {run.test_cmd} plus a hollowing spot-check: a verifier that only trusts the builder's word is a stamp, not a check). The red node commits the test file but nothing passes yet BY DESIGN - a run stopped between red and green leaves a committed failing test, so resume or stop deliberately, never by accident. Commits are the nodes' job inside {run.repo_dir} only; the verifier commits nothing. Tiers: worker for red and green, manager for verify.

defaults.context: You are one lane of a test-first slice. Ground rules: touch only {run.repo_dir}; the test is the contract - changing it to fit the code is forbidden; run the repo's real test command, never an invented substitute; report real observed output, not intent; keep the answer to the schema; one fenced json block as the final message; never print secrets.

nodes.goal: In {run.repo_dir}, implement the MINIMUM needed to turn the red test(s) from your Inputs green. Do not modify or delete the test; do not add features beyond the slice; refactor only where the new code demands it. Run {run.test_cmd}; everything must be green, the new test included. Commit the implementation (separate commit from the test). Reply with ONLY fenced json {"green": <true only on a real full-suite exit 0>, "changed_files": ["<repo-relative paths committed>"], "evidence": "<one line: the summary line of the real test run>"}

Independent verification of the slice in {run.repo_dir}. Trust NOTHING in your Inputs' self-reports: 1) re-run {run.test_cmd} yourself and observe the real exit code; 2) spot-check the test is not hollow - temporarily break the new implementation line by line (or stub it) and confirm the test goes red again, then restore EXACTLY (git diff must show your scratch undone); 3) confirm the diff commits nothing beyond test + implementation for this slice. verified=true only when all three hold. Commit nothing. Reply with ONLY fenced json {"verified": <bool>, "note": "<what you ran, what you broke and saw, final git status line>"}
